text: Welcome to the Beginner Capstone. Over these ten lessons you're going to take one real stakeholder request at Driftwood Media, and carry it all the way from a vague Slack message to a published Power BI report, with real Snowflake SQL at every step.

Here's where we pick up. Driftwood's VP of Support messages you directly: can you just show me how many tickets we're getting each day this month, broken down by priority? I want to glance at it before Monday's leadership sync. Sounds easy. It isn't yet, because four pieces of that sentence are each hiding a real question. How many tickets — every ticket, or just real customer ones? Each day this month — month to date, or the whole month? By priority — all four levels, even on a day with zero urgent tickets? And before Monday — does this need to refresh on its own, or is one answer enough?

The fix is the same short follow-up conversation every reporting ask needs: nail down the time window, the scope, the metric, and the grain — the level of detail each row represents. Here that's one row per calendar day, per priority level.

Once you ask, the vague request turns into something specific: a report showing the count of support tickets created each day this month, broken out by priority, refreshable on demand, for the VP of Support. That sentence is the real spec for this entire project — specific enough that a teammate could read it and build the same thing.

Just as important as what's in scope is what's deliberately left out, for now. In scope: one raw table, one SQL view, one Power BI connection. Not yet: dbt, Airflow, multi-role masking, anything real-time. Those tools earn their place once Driftwood has more stakeholders and more sources to coordinate — that's the Intermediate project, not this one.

That's the business ask, turned into a real requirement. Next lesson, we plan the actual Snowflake setup this requirement needs — the warehouse, the stage, the load, the query, the view, and the one role that gets to read it — sketched out in plain English before a single real object gets created.
